name: US jobless claims
summary: US initial jobless claims 200,000 in the week to 7 Nov; 4-week average 195,250, at its 52-week low
state: Initial US jobless claims were 200,000 in the week to 7 Nov, above the 195,000 expected, and continuing claims were 1.697 million (Rio Times, 13 Nov). The four-week average of 195,250 is at its 52-week low, far below the 15% Watch line. October payrolls rose 165,000 against a 65,000 forecast, with unemployment at 4.1%. The next weekly claims figures are due on 19 Nov.
for_you: Low layoffs mean the US jobs market remains firm, which supports household incomes. It also tends to keep pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates to slow inflation.
rubric_hit: Normal: 4-week average 195,250 is 0% above its 52-week low (< 15% Watch line)

sources.title: Rio Times — US 10-Year Yield Tops 5% as Gold Drops 2.5%

why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.
